rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who turn away are like the dead because they gain no benefit from the extraordinary signs they see and hear.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المعرض قد ساوى الميت في حاله التي هي عدم الانتفاع بما يرى ويسمع من الخوارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal expression stresses that the Prophet has no power to make them hear by himself, apart from God's enabling him.
rows.anchor: معبرًا بالأسمية تنبيها على عدم إثبات ذلك له صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves are physical and metaphorical; only God can grant hearing that benefits them, if He wills, so the Prophet need not grieve over them.
rows.anchor: بل الله يسمعهم إن شاء فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is evidence for resurrection.
rows.anchor: والآية دليل على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's role is to awaken dead hearts with warnings, not to compel people to believe or act as their controller.
rows.anchor: أي تنبه القلوب الميتة بقوارع الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent with truth that is firmly established and matches reality; the abundance of proofs confirms that correspondence.
rows.anchor: الأمر الكامل في الثبات الذي يطابقه الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun in بالحق indicates that the message is true and that both the Sender and the messenger are truthful.
rows.anchor: كلا من المرسل والرسول محق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet brings glad tidings to the obedient and warning to the disobedient.
rows.anchor: بشيرا } أي لمن أطاع { ونذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining the two descriptions with waw signals that the Prophet is fully grounded in both roles.
rows.anchor: والعطف بالواو للدلالة على العراقة في كل من الصفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every earlier nation received a warner, directly or through surviving prophetic teachings, words, deeds, customs, and the testimony of reason.
rows.anchor: إما بنفسه وإما بما ابقى في أعقابهم من شرائعه من أقواله وأفعاله ورسومه مع ما لهم من العقول الشاهدة بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse mentions warning to console the Prophet through its hardship; some earlier prophets had only a warning mission because no one followed them to benefit from glad tidings.
rows.anchor: ولأن من الأنبياء الماضين عليهم السلام من تمحضت دعوته للنذارة لأنه لم ينتفع أحد ببشارته لعدم اتباع أحد منهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denials of earlier peoples console the Prophet, who grieved for his people and feared that their rejection reflected a shortcoming in his own conduct.
rows.anchor: ولما كان صلى الله عليه وسلم شديد الأسف على إبائهم رحمة لهم وخوفا من أن يكون ذلك لتقصير في حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the people reject the Prophet, they follow earlier peoples who rejected what their messengers brought from God.
rows.anchor: أي ما أتتهم به رسلهم عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers brought clear signs demonstrating the truth of their missions.
rows.anchor: الآيات الواضحات في الدلالة على صحة الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-zubur are written materials, including scriptures, traditions, and teachings.
rows.anchor: الأمور المكتوبة من الصحف ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book means the category of scripture, such as the Torah and Gospel; the clarifying Book makes the paths of good and evil plain, as the Prophet's scripture does more fully.
rows.anchor: أي جنس الكتاب كالتوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After consoling the Prophet, God warns those who oppose him by recalling how He seized earlier deniers after the messengers had patiently called them.
rows.anchor: هدد من خالفه وعصاه بما فعل في تلك الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ثم points to long reprieve, which should lead to repentance rather than false confidence that punishment has been forgotten.
rows.anchor: مشيرا بأداة التراخي إلى أن طول الإمهال ينبغي أن يكون سببا للإنابة لا للاغترار بظن الإهمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about God's denunciation of them conveys the horror and magnitude of the punishments that befell those peoples.
rows.anchor: إنكار يجب السؤال عن كيفية لهوله وعظمه

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri warns that if they persist in their wayward course, God's established practice of vengeance and disgrace will not change.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : ولئن أصروا على سنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One thing can bring guidance and happiness to some people and misguidance and misery to others, a subtle sign of God's complete power and oneness.
rows.anchor: شيء واحد سببا لسعادة قوم وهداهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of God's greatest name gives weight to what follows.
rows.anchor: ولفت القول إلى الاسم الأعظم دلالة على عظمة ما في حيزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of majesty in فأخرجنا stresses God's grandeur.
rows.anchor: أي بما لنا من العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits differ in kinds, colors, forms, and natures despite coming from the same water, demonstrating God's power to differentiate them.
rows.anchor: ألوان أنواعها وأصنافها وهيئاتها وطبائعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No creature can distinguish the water into what suits each different product; this power belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: فلا قدرة لغيره سبحانه على تمييز شيء منه إلى ما يصلح لشيء دون آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As one water yields fruits that differ, the same scriptural proofs can become light for one person and blindness for another.
rows.anchor: لا يستبعد عليه أن يجعل الدلائل بالكتاب وغيره نورا لشخص وعمى لآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains are the hardest and least receptive part of the earth, and the water has no effect on them, so they are introduced separately from the fruits.
rows.anchor: ذاكرا ما هو أصلب الأرض وأبعدها عن قابلية التأثر وقطعه عن الأول لأن الماء لا تأثير له فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain judad are paths, landmarks, and intersecting lines, including white and red bands.
rows.anchor: أي طرائق وعلامات وخطوط متقاطعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The colors of these mountain paths are unusually enduring and do not fade over long periods, unlike most old things.
rows.anchor: أنها لا تخلق ولا تضمحل ألوانها على طول الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word judad has several related senses: earth's surface, a path or marker, a contrasting line on a donkey's back, hard level ground, and level ground generally.
rows.anchor: الأرض المستوية . ولما كان أبلغ من ذلك أن تلك الطرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white and red bands vary in shade within each color, since neither is completely pure, though they arise from one earth.
rows.anchor: وهي من الأرض وهي واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root gharaba carries the sense of hiddenness or obscurity, associated with sunset and hence with blackness; gharībīb intensifies the meaning of very black.
rows.anchor: تدور على الخفاء الذي يلزمه الغموض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The understood wording is سود غرابيب سود; the first سود is omitted so the emphatic وصف precedes its dependent and then is reiterated for maximal emphasis.
rows.anchor: ( وسود غرابيب سود ) فأضمر الأول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glossed gharībīb as the most intense blackness; al-Bukhari transmitted the statement from him.
rows.anchor: قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أشد سواد الغرابيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure black ground is rare; the author compares it to dye without other colors, found around Fuwah, Masir, and nearby parts of Egypt.
rows.anchor: لأن السواد الخالص في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dawābb originally includes anything that creeps on earth, then commonly refers to riding animals; livestock is added to explicitly include all kinds.
rows.anchor: في الأصل لما دب على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The colors of the people, creatures, and livestock differ like the fruits and mountain paths; one underlying earth has homogeneous substances but varying qualities, against natural causation.
rows.anchor: { كذلك } أي مثل الثمار والأراضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variety in creation proves God acts by choice and can make one thing light for some and blindness for others; this leads to asking who truly fears Him and excludes the possibility of an ignorant saint.
rows.anchor: ثبت بهذا البرهان أنه سبحانه فاعل الاختيار

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the well-known reading, God is the object and the scholars are the subject: only scholars fear God, because fear requires knowledge.
rows.anchor: إنما ينفع الإنذار أهل الخشية

rows.speaker: السهرودي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says that anyone who does not fear God lacks knowledge; the scholar is a jurist who acts on what he knows.
rows.anchor: قال السهرودي في الباب الثالث من عوارفه

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the alternate reading, the author invokes reciprocal reverence: scholars honor God, and God honors them for their knowledge.
rows.anchor: سبب إجلالهم له إجلاله لهم

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: محمد بن القاياتي
rows.claim: Asked how to understand the alternate reading, al-Qayati answered with a poetic example of revering a beloved who has no power over the speaker.
rows.anchor: محمد بن القاياتي عن توجيه هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty and over all affairs; the contrasts in creation show that nothing He wills is difficult, and His might inspires fear.
rows.anchor: أي المحيط بالجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description as forgiving encourages those who turn their hearts to God, since He can erase their sins.
rows.anchor: في أنه يمحو ذنوب من يريد منهم فيقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who truly fear God preserve the Book through ongoing recitation, whether or not they understand it.
rows.anchor: يجددون التلاوة كل وقت مستمرين على ذلك محافظين عليه كلما نزل من القرآن شيء وبعد كمال نزوله حتى يكون ذلك ديدنهم وشأنهم بفهم وبغير فهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compared the Quran's tendency to slip from memory to camels escaping their tethers; Muslim reports this from Abu Musa al-Ashari, with no grading stated here.
rows.anchor: أخرجه مسلم عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing and lets worshippers converse with God through His Book.
rows.anchor: وهي الناهية عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They spend from what God alone has provided, for all that pleases Him, privately and publicly, persevering even if their wealth runs out.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أن الرزق منه وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation is present tense to convey repeated devotion as revelation arrived and continued study; prayer and spending are past tense to urge prompt action and mark its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: وفي الثاني والثالث بالماضي حثا على المبادرة إلى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation, prayer, and spending give evidence through the tongue, body, and wealth for the heart's fear of God.
rows.anchor: جعل لفعل القلب الذي هو الخشية دليلا باللسان وآخر بالإركان وثالثا بالأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expect an enduring trade in this life and the next, made from their deeds and incapable of loss or collapse.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا والآخرة { تجارة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their trade is safe and profitable because it is entrusted to God, who never loses deposits and possesses perfect power, knowledge, and wealth.
rows.anchor: من لا تضيع لديه الودائع وهي رائجة رابحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are the outcome of God's prior grace and can also be read as a substitute explaining that grace.
rows.anchor: مسببة عن سبب السبق الذي هو الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn means permanent residence without departure, since nothing makes the inhabitants leave.
rows.anchor: أي إقامة بلا رحيل لأنه لا سبب

rows.speaker: قراء الجماعة
rows.claim: On the active reading used by the majority, the pronoun can refer to all three groups; some take it as referring to God's chosen servants and limit entry to the moderate and foremost.
rows.anchor: بفتح الياء وضم الخاء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: On Abu Amr's passive reading, the pronoun refers only to the foremost; they linger on musk platforms and are then led to Paradise when called.
rows.anchor: البناء للمفعول يكون الضمير للسابق فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those admitted to Paradise never leave because nothing can expel them and they themselves have no desire to depart.
rows.anchor: ومن دخلها لم يخرج منها لأنه لا شيء يخرجه ولا هو يريد الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage first mentions bracelets generally and then specifies their materials, using delayed clarification to heighten anticipation.
rows.anchor: للإبهام ثم البيان مزيد روعة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants wear gold bracelets and pearls as adornment.
rows.anchor: أي يلبسون على سبيل التزين والتحلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their clothing is silk, fitting the splendid adornment they wear on entering Paradise.
rows.anchor: لا تليق إلى على اللباس الفاخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their past-tense praise at entry presents the removal of sorrow as accomplished and certain.
rows.anchor: أي عند دخولهم : { الحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God removes every kind of sorrow; they will never grieve again because nothing is lost or extinguished in the lasting abode.
rows.anchor: فلا نحزن على شيء كان فاتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing their faults could have led them to Hell without divine generosity, they credit their outcome to God's forgiveness and rewarding gratitude.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إلينا مع إساءتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No servant has a claim against the Master; the inhabitants enter by grace, since their good deeds themselves were gifts God enabled.
rows.anchor: بلا عمل منا فإن حسناتنا إنما كانت منا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode of permanence is a place and time of settled residence; no one wants or is made to leave, and nothing disappears to cause regret.
rows.anchor: أي الإقامة ومكانها وزمانها التي لا يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling the terrors and burdens of Judgment, they describe Paradise as free from physical hardship and exhaustion.
rows.anchor: ما شاهدوه في عرصات القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naṣab is bodily strain, pain, or illness; lughūb is weariness, fatigue, or slackness of spirit.
rows.anchor: نصب بدن ولا وجع ولا شيء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says languor follows from bodily fatigue.
rows.anchor: أبو حيان : هو لازم من تعب البدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's image says sorrow cannot enter the place of bliss, even if a stone touched it and became happiness.
rows.anchor: علينا لا تنزل الأحزان شاحتها لو مسحها حجر مسته سراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are those who concealed the clear signs their reason disclosed and treated God's allies and callers to Him with arrogance.
rows.anchor: ما دلت عليه عقولهم من شموس الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike ordinary fire, Hell does not finish them off by a ruling that brings death, increasing their punishment.
rows.anchor: زيادة في نكالهم وسوء مآلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neither die nor receive any easing of Hell's punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يحكم وينفذ ويثبت من حاكم ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing messengerhood and its glad tidings, the passage turns to resurrection, which helps affirm God's oneness and consoles believers who suffer in worldly life.
rows.anchor: الأصل الثاني هو الرسالة واتبعها ثمرتها المختومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic plural of majesty announces the grandeur of these purposes and that only the Majestic can protect the small, distinct group of believers.
rows.anchor: إلى مظهر العظمة إيذانا بعظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revives the dead gradually in this life and all together at the Hour, physically through resurrection and spiritually by rescuing whom He wills from obscurity.
rows.anchor: أي بحسب التدريج الآن وجملة في الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people send ahead includes all their actions, states, and words, recorded together when the spirit is breathed.
rows.anchor: من جميع أفعالهم وأحوالهم وأقوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their آثار are the practices they leave behind, good or bad; each person is repaid for them in the unending afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي سنتهم التي تبقى من بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To show that the record covers more than human deeds and that God needs no external aid, He says that He encompasses every created and uncreated matter in eternal knowledge and writing.
rows.anchor: أي من أمر الأحياء وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear Imam is a fitting book to consult, in which no circumstance is hidden from anyone seeking its knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي كتاب هو أهل لأن يقصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by mutual implication: the verb implies enumeration, while Imam implies the act of writing.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : دل فعل الإحصاء على مصدره وذكر الإمام على فعل الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is presented after the sign of daytime as the corresponding sign of night.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر آية النهار , أتبعها آية الليل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وروح عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Rawh from Yaqub read al-qamar in the nominative, yielding the sense that it runs toward its appointed place.
rows.anchor: ومعناه في قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو وروح عن يعقوب بالرفع : يجري لمستقر له

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers put al-qamar in the accusative, emphasizing the grandeur and speed of its course; it covers in a month what the sun covers in a year.
rows.anchor: ونصبه الباقون دلالة على عظمة هذا الجري لسرعته بقطعه في شهر ما تقطعه الشمس في سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God measured the moon's course through twenty-eight stations; it then disappears for two nights at month's completion or one night as the month wanes.
rows.anchor: أي قسناه قياسا عظيما أي قسنا

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri describes the moon moving away from the sun until full, then drawing near it and waning until it disappears.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري : يبعد عن الشمس ولا يزال يتباعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿurjūn is the date-palm stalk from the bunch's branches to its tip, thin and curved as it projects from the palm.
rows.anchor: من النخل وهو عود العذق ما بين شماريخه إلى منتهاه وهو منتبه من النخلة دقيقا منحنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun ʿurjūn is on the faʿlūl pattern; lexicographers connect the verb ʿarjana with depicting palm stalks on cloth, while commentators derive it from ʿaraja, to bend.
rows.anchor: وهو فعلول ذكره أهل اللغة في النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Old means weathered: a palm stalk becomes thin, bent, and yellow over time, matching the moon's reddish-yellow hue.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت حمرته آخذة إلى صفرة

words: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each luminary has fixed stations and cannot displace the other's sign; when one appears the other recedes, and their convergence marks the Hour.
rows.anchor: لكل منهما منازل لا يعدوها

words: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the ordered cosmos the sun cannot overtake and obliterate the moon, nor can the fast-moving moon overtake the sun so that day disappears.
rows.anchor: ما دام هذا الكون موجودا على هذا الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night does not precede or overtake day; the moon's faster movement never catches the sun and removes daylight altogether.
rows.anchor: أي حتى ينبغي للقمر مع سرعة سيره
